verdict.rationale: SharePoint documents first-party webhooks: apps can subscribe to notifications when a SharePoint list changes, without polling. The docs also spell out retry semantics (up to 5 delivery retries on error) and mention a value usable for validating notifications. The evidence ties notifications to list changes rather than explicitly to file/document events, and the verification mechanism appears only as a passing mention, so the story's 'file events' and 'verification spelled out' elements are only partly covered. missing for 10: explicit evidence that file/document-library changes trigger notifications, a documented subscription validation handshake and verification flow, notification payload details, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, file events push to me — documented webhooks/change notifications fire when content changes, with verification and retry semantics spelled out

citations.quote: SharePoint webhooks enable developers to build applications that subscribe to receive notifications on specific events that occur in SharePoint.
SharePoint webhooks provide a simple notification pipeline so that your application can be aware of changes to a SharePoint list without polling the service.
You can use this for validating notifications, tagging different subscriptions, or other reasons.
If an error occurs while sending the notification to your application, SharePoint retries up to 5 times to deliver the notification.
